the-singular-command-line-is-the-registr.text: The Singular command line is the registry; the open datum is its own executable.

As the author of an application (the open datum today, cardano-keri next), I build one executable against the Singular library. It accepts Singular's common flags unchanged, defines its own verbs, mints its own approval assets, has the library build and book the request around them, folds when I ask, and never touches singular registry code.

As an operator of a registry, I run singular registry create | fold | reject | reclaim | inspect and nothing else. The open datum's insert, update and terminate (and its own create, fold and inspect) are commands of the open-datum executable.
As Bob, when I book a registration for a key that is already active, the booking is refused before I sign, with a named reason, and I pay nothing.

rulings-in-force.text: Planning ruling (desk, 2026-10-09): the CLI split (#528) builds against the library's request and fold, not the open-datum envelope.

Operator, 2026-10-08: "the only real singular CLI is registry"; the application binary links Singular up to the command-line layer so Singular's flags pass through. Cleanup: code moves, behaviour does not change (the one addition is the early booking refusal below).

Desk ruling A-001, 2026-10-09: singular links no application code. The open-datum executable's verbs are create, insert, update, terminate, fold and inspect; the last three are thin calls to the library with its application value. singular registry fold folds what needs no application and refuses a termination with a message naming the application's executable. singular registry create pins a policy given as a hash. The import control covers the libraries and singular's Main alike. Demo 1's scripts and control journeys change binaries in the same PR.

Desk ruling A-002 (epic 396), 2026-10-09: #486 is delivered here, written once in the library's request building. --fold stays on the open-datum executable's insert and terminate; #486's "remove the combined switch" is superseded.
Request datum inline, no size cap (2026-10-09). The request tag is #529, not here.
Staffing ruling 2026-10-09: ticket owner Claude Sonnet 5.5, commit owner Muse, mute persistent auditor GLM; no other seat.

Operator amendment, 2026-10-10 (released by the desk): "make sure the 2 applications live in completely separated hierarchies", on-chain and off-chain. Each application owns one top-level tree: applications/open-datum/ and applications/keri-stub/. Everything of an application lives in its tree: Lean, on-chain sources in its own Aiken project, off-chain sources in its own cabal package (library, executable, tests), scripts and fixtures. offchain/ and onchain/ hold the registry only. Dependencies point one way: an application depends on the registry packages; the registry never depends on an application; neither application references the other's tree. Every validator hash and published identity is unchanged by the move.

Lean binding: the model does not change. Lean tree d9161edd0274b67151f331949521f34bbf18612f, onchain validators tree 232c5cbaf94a03eb313e72f83287a05a944511b7, constitution 1.14.0, all at base e3c9ab01. No validator logic, script hash or Lean file changes; the open-datum validators move to the application's Aiken project and every hash stays byte-identical.

acceptance.text: Every item names the check that proves it. A check is an existing hosted job or a control this ticket adds to one (marked new control).

[ ] singular accepts only registry create | fold | reject | reclaim | inspect; the parser, --help and the docs name nothing else. Proof: the unit specs for the command line (cage-tests, tag [cli]), the documented-flags job (cli-flags: cli-flags-check, cli-flags-controls), plus new control: singular registry insert, update and terminate are each refused as an unknown command, run in the same job.

[ ] No module of the registry libraries, the registry command-line library or singular's Main imports the open-datum package, and none of those components lists it as a dependency. Proof: new control application-boundary-check and application-boundary-controls (offchain flake apps, new steps of the offchain-component-build job); the controls plant an import and a dependency and must fail.

[ ] The library exports request building around assets the application mints in the same transaction (the approval under its policy) plus destination, datum and deposit; fold, reject and reclaim as library calls; the common session, funding, signing, journal and receipt machinery; and one flag group (--state-token, --koios-url, --network-magic, --wallet-skey, --wallet-address, --preview, --receipt, funding limits) included verbatim by each binary. Proof: cage-tests [cli] specs parse the same flag group through both binaries; offchain-component-build builds both.

[ ] create takes the application policy it pins as an input: from the open-datum executable's application value, or as a hash (--application-policy) for an application whose script does not depend on the registry identity; never as a compiled-in choice. inspect prints raw datums and decodes an output only through an application-supplied decoder. Proof: cage-tests [cli] and [application] specs; Demo 1 create and inspect rows.

[ ] singular registry fold folds an insertion, and refuses a termination with a message that names the application's executable; open-datum fold folds that termination. Proof: Demo 1 refusals job (demo1-cli-controls), new rows.

[ ] The open datum is an executable of its own, built from its own tree applications/open-datum/ against the registry packages, with create, insert, update, terminate, fold and inspect; insert and terminate accept --fold. Proof: offchain-component-build, demo1-cli-check.

[ ] The registry trees hold no application: no file under offchain/ or onchain/ names an application module, path or validator title. An application's package and Aiken project reach outside their own tree only to depend on the registry packages. Proof: new control application-separation-check and application-separation-controls, which plant a registry-side naming and an application-side reach and must fail.

[ ] Every validator hash is unchanged by the move: the hashes of the registry's Aiken project and of the open datum's Aiken project together equal the hashes of the single project at base. Proof: new control script-hash-comparison against the base hashes recorded in this specification's evidence, which plants a changed hash and must fail; script-identity and blueprint stay green.

[ ] A booking for a key whose current leaf the edge rules out is refused before signing, in preview and submit alike, with a named reason such as Alice is already registered, and leaves no pending request; the refusal is labelled client policy; the fold keeps validating. This is written once, in the library's request building (#486). Proof: cage-tests [builders] and [application] specs with a failing control on the base; Demo 1 refusals job.

[ ] Every M1 journey that runs today (token-only join, batched fold, reconciliation after interruption, narration, the registry page, the negative host) runs through the two binaries with its receipts unchanged apart from the binary that ran the command. Proof: demo1-cli-check, demo1-two-actor-control, demo1-cli-controls, demo1-readback, journey, the e2e lanes, conformance-* jobs.

[ ] A cardano-keri stub (register, convict, status) built against the library alone, with its own policy, registers and convicts one key on a devnet and folds its own requests; it imports nothing from the open-datum package. Delivered by its own pull request after this one merges (desk ruling PLAN-REVIEWED, additive, no exclusive window); this pull request carries slices 1 to 5. Proof: new job keri-stub in registry.yml, and the import control above applied to the stub.
[ ] The release archive ships singular and open-datum; the Demo 1 rehearsal commands in the docs use the new binaries. Proof: release-artifacts, verify-release-controls, docs-check.

[ ] Lean binding, receipt-derived conformance state and exact-head checks are recorded per the PR template; no Lean file changes and no validator logic changes. Proof: model, script-identity, blueprint, coverage green.

out-of-scope.text: Any validator logic, script hash or Lean change (#505 landed them; #494, #495, #529, #506 follow). Moving a validator's source file to the application's project is in scope; changing what it compiles to is not.
The request tag (#529); protected rejection (#494, #495); the second application's real integration (cardano-keri's own repository); the naming application (M3, #174).

Concurrent booking (#518, #519), creation funding (#406, #478), recovery journal (#477), forbidden actions (#358), restoration (#471) and join (#485, #381): their behaviour is not touched. Where their files collide, the desk orders the merge.
A runtime plugin protocol. Applications link the library.
Removing --fold (#486's fourth requirement, superseded by A-002).

evidence-this-ticket-produces.text: Receipts and the hosted jobs above are the evidence. Left uncovered, stated in the PR body: the ordering against #485, #471 and #381 until the desk grants the exclusive window; the stub is evidence that the library needs nothing from the open datum, not a cardano-keri deliverable; singular no longer derives the application pin, so for a registry it reads the pin from the state datum it attaches to and compares the three witness pins as before.
